risks.title: Working-tree runtime has debug mode + local environment enabled while spatie/laravel-ignition (dev) is installed, exposing _ignition routes that can execute 'solutions'
risks.evidence: `php artisan about` on the repo-mounted container reports Environment=local, Debug Mode=ENABLED; `php artisan route:list --json` in the same container lists _ignition/execute-solution, _ignition/update-config and _ignition/health-check. vendor/spatie/laravel-ignition/src/IgnitionServiceProvider.php:61 calls registerRoutes() unconditionally, :211-213 loadRoutesFrom(ignition-routes.php) which registers ExecuteSolutionController/UpdateConfigController under middleware RunnableSolutionsEnabled (vendor/.../ignition-routes.php:9-22); vendor/.../Http/Middleware/RunnableSolutionsEnabled.php:12-15 only aborts 404 when RunnableSolutionsGuard::check() fails (debug+local gated).
risks.why_it_may_not_be_exploitable: Production images install with --no-dev (Dockerfile:9, Dockerfile-ARM64:31); route:list inside dujiaoka:2.1.0-php83 shows 0 _ignition routes and vendor/spatie/laravel-ignition is absent from the image. Exploitation requires an operator to install dev dependencies and enable debug in a reachable environment.
risks.recommendation: Keep APP_ENV=production/APP_DEBUG=false in every reachable deployment (.env.example:2,4 defaults are safe) and never run `composer install` without --no-dev on production hosts. Re-verify with `php artisan route:list | grep _ignition` on deployed instances.

risks.title: Admin panel is a dcat/laravel-admin fork consumed from a mutable third-party git repository, pinned only by composer.lock reference
risks.evidence: composer.json:10-14 adds repository https://github.com/Cecil98/dcat-admin and composer.json:19 requires exact '2.2.5'; composer.lock records dcat/laravel-admin source reference 8ff1f8225351824f454f57388e8be812e3870407. The fork is not covered by Packagist advisories (`composer audit` returns advisories: [] for the whole tree) and `composer validate` warns about the exact version constraint.
risks.why_it_may_not_be_exploitable: The currently installed commit is frozen in composer.lock and the shipped image is built from that lock, so today's artifacts are deterministic. Risk materialises on `composer update` or on losing the lock.
risks.recommendation: Pin the fork by commit (`dev-master#<sha>`) or vendor the source; review fork diffs versus upstream 2.2.5 before upgrades; track advisories for the fork manually.

risks.title: Base images and PHP patch level are unpinned; some locally built images are stale relative to the Dockerfile (php hardening ini missing)
risks.evidence: Dockerfile:1 `FROM webdevops/php-nginx:8.3` (mutable tag, no digest); Dockerfile-ARM64:1 `FROM alpine:3.20` with `apk add php83-*` packages (Dockerfile-ARM64:10-14) so the PHP patch level floats with the Alpine repo; Dockerfile-ARM64:27 `COPY --from=composer:2` unpinned. `docker run dujiaoka-php83-final:latest ls /usr/local/etc/php/conf.d | grep dujiaoka` returns no zz-dujiaoka.ini although the nginx security include is present, while dujiaoka:2.1.0-php83 contains both — the -final/-test tags predate Dockerfile:20.
risks.why_it_may_not_be_exploitable: The image tag actually deployed (dujiaoka:2.1.0-php83) does contain the hardened php.ini. Reproducibility rather than immediate exploitability is the primary issue.
risks.recommendation: Pin base images by digest, rebuild and retag ALL published tags from the current Dockerfile, and add a CI assertion that zz-dujiaoka.ini + 20-dujiaoka-security.conf exist in the built image.

risks.title: Project php.ini hardening is minimal: secure cookie flag, SameSite and use_strict_mode are not enforced at the PHP layer
risks.evidence: conf/php.ini:1-8 sets only expose_php=Off and session.cookie_httponly=1; no session.cookie_secure, session.samesite, session.use_strict_mode, display_errors or disable_functions entries. Application defaults: config/session.php:169 'secure' => env('SESSION_SECURE_COOKIE', null), config/session.php:197 'same_site' => env('SESSION_SAME_SITE','lax'), .env.example:69 SESSION_SECURE_COOKIE=false. Effective ini inside the base webdevops image (no project ini): session.cookie_httponly=Off, session.cookie_secure=Off, session.use_strict_mode=Off.
risks.why_it_may_not_be_exploitable: httponly is applied via the project ini and SameSite=lax is the framework default; missing Secure only matters when ADMIN_HTTPS/HTTPS termination is misconfigured, and Laravel's cookie encryption reduces tampering impact. Full determination belongs to security-config/session recon.
risks.recommendation: Add session.cookie_secure=1, session.samesite=Lax/Strict, session.use_strict_mode=1 to conf/php.ini (or document mandatory env values) and set SESSION_SECURE_COOKIE=true in HTTPS deployments.

risks.title: Production defaults expose the dcat admin panel on the well-known /admin path when ADMIN_ROUTE_PREFIX is unset
risks.evidence: config/admin.php:70 'prefix' => env('ADMIN_ROUTE_PREFIX', 'admin'); the shipped image has no /app/.env (Dockerfile-ARM64:34, verified absent in dujiaoka:2.1.0-php83) and `php artisan route:list --json` inside that image shows 95 routes under the `admin` prefix with middleware admin + admin.force-password.
risks.why_it_may_not_be_exploitable: Admin routes are behind dcat's auth middleware plus a rate-limited login and forced password change; predictable path only aids discovery/scanning.
risks.recommendation: Require ADMIN_ROUTE_PREFIX to be set to a non-default value in production deployment docs and enforce it in deploy checks.

risks.title: Abandoned dependency in the production tree (box/spout via dcat/easy-excel)
risks.evidence: `composer audit --format=json` output: "abandoned": {"box/spout": null}; composer.lock packages[] box/spout v3.3.0; required by dcat/easy-excel 1.1.0.
risks.why_it_may_not_be_exploitable: Abandonment is not a vulnerability by itself; no advisory currently matches, and the package is used for spreadsheet import/export.
risks.recommendation: Track replacements (openspout/openspout) and validate any user-supplied spreadsheet import path in the sink/dynamic phases.

risks.title: Laravel AuthenticateSession middleware is disabled, so session IDs are not invalidated on password change
risks.evidence: app/Http/Kernel.php:39 shows `// \Illuminate\Session\Middleware\AuthenticateSession::class,` commented out inside the 'web' group.
risks.why_it_may_not_be_exploitable: Exploitation requires an already-stolen session cookie; framework default is also disabled. Impact is limited to post-password-change session retention.
risks.recommendation: Consider enabling AuthenticateSession or explicitly invalidating sessions on password change; confirm behaviour in the session recon phase.

risks.title: docker-compose publishes PHP-FPM port 9000 on the host alongside HTTP 80
risks.why_it_may_not_be_exploitable: FPM on 9000 is only reachable if the host firewall exposes it; FastCGI requires crafted SCRIPT_FILENAME requests (CVE class for exposed FPM). Whether it is reachable in practice depends on deployment firewall rules, which this static recon cannot verify.
risks.recommendation: Remove the 9000 mapping from the default compose file or bind it to 127.0.0.1; document firewall requirements.
